headline: High-risk shared-workspace and stateful orchestration create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; A is non-runnable but B’s defaults are broad.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable open-source collection with no io_surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B’s outputs. Agent B can read/write files and stdin/stdout, so if an operator manually bridges content into B, prompt injection is possible, but the pathway is unusual and limited by A’s lack of runtime behavior.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-derived text into B’s stdin/stdout or files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to parse untrusted file contents as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Keep A as a static reference only; do not feed its content into B automatically.
Add a manual review step before any A-derived text enters B.
Restrict B to a whitelist of trusted input paths.
Use a prompt delimiter and instruction/content separation policy.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all A-to-B transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, but B has broad network egress, filesystem access, and handles model-provider API keys. If A’s content or operator-provided files are placed into B’s workspace, B can transmit them to third-party model providers by default, creating a realistic leakage path in the pair.
conditions: IF A-derived documents are stored in B’s application-defined files, B can read them.
IF B sends context to model providers, any sensitive content in that context may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive A-derived material in B’s workspace.
Disable or scope B’s outbound model-provider calls for sensitive runs.
Use redaction before any handoff into B.
Separate credentials from B’s working directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data classification gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, while B can write files, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct write-write conflict, but B’s persistent shared-state model means multiple B instances can contend over the same checkpointer store; if A is used as a source of tasks, the pair can still collide on shared mutable resources through B’s orchestration layer.
conditions: IF multiple B instances share the same checkpointer store, state races can occur.
IF A-derived instructions cause B to write the same application files repeatedly, overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Assign each B invocation a unique workspace.
Serialize access to the checkpointer store.
Avoid concurrent writes from multiple B instances.
Keep A outputs read-only and immutable.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated collection with no runtime verification, so its outputs are not authoritative facts. B is a stateful orchestrator that can treat upstream text as node input; if A-derived content is used as guidance without verification, B may propagate stale or incorrect instructions into downstream actions or tool calls.
conditions: IF B consumes A-derived text as authoritative node input, errors can cascade.
IF B’s downstream tools act on unverified instructions, incorrect actions may be executed.
mitigations: Require verification before B acts on A-derived content.
Mark A as reference-only in B’s prompts.
Add a human approval step for any action-producing node.
Log source provenance for each B decision.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in A, and B only states application-defined graph state plus model-provider keys. The pair therefore shows only a limited compliance gap: B’s broad egress and state handling could matter if operators place regulated data into the graph, but that is not established here.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B’s graph state, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF B’s model-provider calls process regulated data, a policy review is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B unless policy-approved.
Review B’s retention settings before use.
Separate secrets from graph state.
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
